product_overview.problem_statement: Everyday DIY investors hear that universities like Yale grew their endowments with a famous investing strategy, but the information is buried in annual-report PDFs and finance jargon. There is no simple place to see how these endowments actually invested, what that strategy looks like rebuilt with ordinary ETFs, and whether it honestly beat simple index investing.

target_users.needs: Manages own retirement/brokerage accounts; curious, not professional; needs plain English with every finance term defined.

success_metrics: All 5 schools browsable in the History Explorer with allocation + returns charts over their disclosed coverage (Stanford: market-value-only per BRD OI-1). Measured by phone-width walkthrough at ship.
Translator works for every school/fiscal-year with disclosed allocation data, with visible proxy mapping and fine print. Measured by rendering every school/year in the DB.
Comparisons render for any school vs. proxy vs. all 3 benchmarks over any sub-period. Measured by exercising period-picker extremes.
Methodology page lists every source_id in the DB; disclaimer visible on every page. Measured by automated check + walkthrough.
Production URL publicly reachable (unauthenticated curl -I returns 200), Lighthouse performance and accessibility pass, works on phone screens.
out_of_scope: BRD-026 depth beyond FY2000 for Yale (could-priority; not pursued — Yale curation starts at FY2000 per TASKS 1.3)
constraints: Education, not advice — no copy tells a user what to do with their money
Plain English, terms defined on first use
Next.js App Router on Vercel + Neon; no backend beyond server components/route handlers
Backtest math requires unit tests with hand-computed expected values
dataviz skill must be read before any chart code

stack.frontend: Next.js 16 (App Router, TypeScript, React 19, Tailwind 4) — server components by default, client components only where interactivity requires
stack.backend: None beyond Next.js server components; no route handlers anticipated (read-only public data, queried server-side)
stack.database: Neon Postgres (serverless HTTP driver @neondatabase/serverless) via Drizzle ORM; schema in src/lib/db/schema.ts
stack.hosting: Vercel Pro (project amay-s-projects3/universityfunds), auto-deploy on push to main, PR preview deployments
stack.ci_cd: Vercel build on push; tests run locally/pre-push (no separate CI configured — see Q-003)
other: Chart library: Recharts (default suggestion, confirm at build per Q-002)

decision_records.decision: App-wide performance default: LCP < 2.5s on a mid-range phone over 4G; Lighthouse performance ≥ 90 and accessibility ≥ 95 on every route
decision_records.rationale: BRD-032 says 'loads fast' without numbers; one quantified default keeps every spec item testable (referenced as 'app perf default').

decision_records.decision: Runtime DB access is read-only; all writes go through seed files + npm run seed
decision_records.rationale: BRD-020: seed files are the single source of truth; anything else forks the truth.

decision_records.decision: Stanford presentation: market value over time only, with plain-English explanation; allocation/returns charts marked unavailable linking to methodology
decision_records.options_considered: Merged Pool with disclaimer; exclude Stanford; unavailable-state only
decision_records.rationale: BRD OI-1, resolved by human 2026-08-03. Merged Pool is ~25% non-endowment with confirmed 2.9pp FY2024 return divergence — showing it as 'Stanford's endowment' would violate BRD-005 honesty.

decision_records.decision: Copycat forward runs use snapshot vintages: a school's last-disclosed mix may be carried forward through full benchmark coverage, labelled e.g. 'Yale's FY2020 mix, held unchanged by this copycat through FY2025' — never 'held since'
decision_records.options_considered: Truncate copycat at last disclosed year; extrapolate allocations
decision_records.rationale: TASKS 4.3 / task-1.3 proxy decision: gives users recent years without inventing allocation data; divergence from the school's actual returns is an honest, interesting result.

decision_records.decision: Charts render allocation coverage ends on the chart itself (boundary marker), not in captions
decision_records.rationale: TASKS 3.2: the returns chart beside it runs to FY2025; the reader notices the mismatch at the chart and needs the explanation there.

decision_records.decision: Proposed (Q-001, default per TASKS 1.7): hedge funds and private equity get no pretend proxy — the copycat covers only the publicly-replicable sleeve, with the remainder shown as an explicit labelled gap
decision_records.options_considered: Investable HF/PE index ETFs (none freely citable back to FY2000); liquid-alt proxies
decision_records.rationale: Those categories are ~half of Yale's portfolio; a fake proxy would be less honest than a visible gap (BRD-005). Final call sits with SPEC-005 curation.

spec_items.title: Database schema and data model (6 tables)
spec_items.summary: Drizzle schema for schools, allocations, endowment_returns, benchmark_returns, proxy_mappings, sources, pushed to Neon. Already built and verified live (TASKS 1.1).
spec_items.detailed_description: Normalized relational model where every fact row carries a source_id foreign key into sources. Category and series identifiers constrained to the constants in src/lib/constants.ts (8 normalized allocation categories; benchmark series sp500, us_aggregate_bond, intl_equity, reit, cash, plus hedge_fund_index, public_pe_index, global_equity pending SPEC-005).

data_entities.retention: Permanent; rows managed solely by seed

fields: source_label: text (school's original wording, keeps normalization auditable)
return_pct: numeric null (null = not published, e.g. Stanford)
etf_ticker: text not null OR explicit no-proxy marker
honesty_note: text null (where proxy is weak)

db_changes: Initial schema push (done, verified live on Neon PostgreSQL 17.10)
migration_steps: drizzle-kit push against Neon (completed; idempotent re-run confirmed 'No changes detected')
spec_items.rollback_plan: Schema is additive-only so far; a rollback is drizzle-kit push of the prior schema.ts from git history. Data restores via re-seed from git-versioned seed files.
acceptance_criteria: Given the live Neon database, When drizzle-kit push runs against src/lib/db/schema.ts, Then it reports no changes (schema and code in sync).
Given any fact row in allocations/endowment_returns/benchmark_returns, When its source_id is looked up, Then a sources row exists (FK enforced or seed-validated).
error_handling: Schema drift between code and DB surfaces at drizzle-kit push — resolve in code, never by editing the DB directly (BRD-020).
spec_items.test_strategy: Verified live per TASKS 1.1 (all 6 tables + columns confirmed on Neon). Ongoing guarantee comes from seed-script validation (SPEC-002) and the data access layer's typed queries (SPEC-007).
qa_signoff_criteria: Already met: tables live, push idempotent (TASKS 1.1 build log).

spec_items.title: Seed script with validation (npm run seed)
spec_items.summary: Reads data/, validates everything before opening a connection, upserts on natural keys, prunes rows deleted from seed files. Already built and verified both ways (TASKS 1.2).
business_rules: Allocations per school-year must sum to ~100% (±0.1 tolerance per DATA-README).
Every row's source_id must exist in sources — no citation, no number (BRD-021).
Nothing is written if any validation check fails (all-or-nothing).
spec_items.rollback_plan: Seed files are git-versioned; rollback = git revert the seed-file change and re-run npm run seed (the script prunes rows removed from files).
acceptance_criteria: Given valid seed files, When npm run seed runs twice, Then the second run is idempotent (no changes).
Given a seed file with an uncited or non-summing row, When npm run seed runs, Then it exits 1 with the specific errors and the DB is untouched.
Given a row deleted from a seed file, When npm run seed runs, Then the corresponding DB row is pruned.
error_handling: Validation failures print row-level errors and exit non-zero before any connection opens; partial writes are impossible by construction.
spec_items.test_strategy: Verified per TASKS 1.2: clean run on empty files, bad fixture rejected with 14 errors/exit 1/DB untouched, re-run idempotent. seed:verify script exercises the validator.
qa_signoff_criteria: Already met (TASKS 1.2 build log).

spec_items.title: Curated dataset: 5 schools + benchmark series, FY2000–FY2025
spec_items.summary: Hand-curated, cited, QC-verified seed data for Yale, Harvard, MIT, Princeton, Stanford plus 5 complete benchmark series, seeded to Neon. Already done (TASKS 1.3–1.6) with documented per-school coverage limits.
spec_items.detailed_description: Coverage as verified: Yale returns/market values FY2000–FY2025, allocations FY2000–FY2020 (Yale stopped publishing the table after 2020). Harvard allocations 77 rows FY2005–FY2025 (FY2018/FY2022 never published), returns/market values complete FY2000–FY2025. Princeton 104 allocation rows + 24 return rows. MIT 42 allocation rows (sparse — pool-basis and congressional-response years) + complete 26-year returns. Stanford market values only FY2000–FY2025 (Aug-31 FY), allocations/returns a documented structural gap (Merged Pool ≠ Endowment; BRD OI-1). Benchmarks: sp500, us_aggregate_bond, intl_equity, reit, cash complete FY2000–FY2025; hedge_fund_index, public_pe_index, global_equity deliberately empty pending SPEC-005.
assumptions: BRD-026 (deeper Yale history, could-priority) intentionally not pursued; recorded in product_overview.out_of_scope.
spec_items.rollback_plan: Seed files are git-versioned; any data correction is a seed-file edit + re-seed.
acceptance_criteria: Given the seeded database, When any allocation school-year is summed, Then it totals 100 ±0.1.
Given any curated number, When traced via source_id, Then a primary-document citation exists.
Given the 60/40 composite, When compared to Vanguard's balanced index fund FY2000–FY2025, Then all 26 years agree within ~1pp (verified in TASKS 1.4).
error_handling: Data corrections follow the seed-file workflow only; per-school coverage gaps are displayed honestly downstream (SPEC-010/012), never interpolated.
spec_items.test_strategy: Verified via curation QC: spot-checks against independently re-fetched primary documents, sums recomputed, MIT returns verified by compounding against 7 published windows, idempotent re-seed (TASKS 1.3–1.6).
qa_signoff_criteria: Already met (TASKS 1.3–1.6 build logs and DATA-README).

spec_items.title: ETF proxy-mapping curation + final three benchmark series (task 1.7)
spec_items.summary: Curate proxy_mappings (each allocation category → ETF ticker + plain-English rationale + honesty note where weak) and decide/seed the three deliberately-empty benchmark series (hedge_fund_index, public_pe_index, global_equity). The benchmark series and the ETF proxy for a category must be the same instrument or the copycat comparison is incoherent.
spec_items.detailed_description: Every category used in any school's allocations gets a mapping or a documented reason it has none. Front-runner for global_equity: Vanguard Total World (VT/VTWSX), first full fiscal year FY2009, which covers every year currently needed. For hedge funds and private equity (~half of Yale's portfolio in many years) no freely-citable investable series reaches back to FY2000; the proposed default (Q-001) is the explicit-gap sleeve: the copycat covers only the publicly-replicable sleeve and shows the remainder as a labelled gap. Carry forward the honesty note that reit is listed real estate only.
business_rules: Proxy instrument and benchmark series for a category must be the identical instrument.
Every ETF chosen must be ordinary and widely available (standard US brokerage, no accreditation/minimums — BRD assumption 4).
Every mapping row: ticker + one-sentence plain-English rationale + honesty note where the proxy is weak.
No number enters seed files without a citation (BRD-021).
edge_cases: Category present in one school's allocations but no others
Category with no honest proxy (hedge funds, PE, venture) — explicit-gap marker, never a pretend proxy
ETF inception later than FY2000 — document first covered fiscal year per series
db_changes: New rows in proxy_mappings and benchmark_returns via seed files (no schema change)
spec_items.rollback_plan: git revert the seed-file commit and re-seed (script prunes removed rows).
acceptance_criteria: Given every category used in any school's allocations, When proxy_mappings is queried, Then each has an ETF mapping or a documented no-proxy reason.
Given each mapped category, When its benchmark series is compared to its ETF proxy, Then they are the same instrument.
Given the seeded series, When npm run seed re-runs, Then it is idempotent and all validations pass.
error_handling: If no honest instrument exists for a category, record the explicit-gap decision in proxy_mappings and DATA-README rather than forcing a weak proxy.
spec_items.test_strategy: Seed validation (SPEC-002) plus a curation QC pass: spot-check each chosen instrument's fiscal-year returns against an independent source; verify coverage windows documented per series.
spec_items.test_data_requirements: None beyond the seed files themselves.
qa_signoff_criteria: All acceptance criteria green
DATA-README updated with instruments, coverage windows, and the sleeve decision
TASKS 1.7 checked off with build-log note
spec_items.hypercare_watch: None at runtime — data correctness is locked at seed time.

spec_items.title: Site shell: header/nav, footer with disclaimer, responsive, dark-mode friendly
spec_items.summary: App-wide layout with nav (Explore, Compare, Methodology), a footer disclaimer visible on every page, responsive from phone width up, dark-mode friendly, plain-English tone.
user_stories: As a DIY investor, I want clear navigation and an always-visible reminder that this is education not advice, so that I can explore without being misled about what the site is.
main_flow: 1. Any route renders inside the shared layout
2. Header shows site name + nav links: Explore, Compare, Methodology
3. Footer shows the education-not-advice disclaimer on every page
4. Layout adapts phone → desktop; honors prefers-color-scheme
business_rules: Disclaimer text must state the site is educational, not financial advice, and is never hidden or collapsed (BRD-003).
edge_cases: Very narrow screens (320px)
Long school names in nav context
No-JS render (server components should still produce full HTML)
error_handling: A route-level error boundary shows a plain-English error page that keeps header/footer (and thus the disclaimer) visible.
acceptance_criteria: Given any route in the app, When it renders, Then header nav and footer disclaimer are present.
Given a 320px-wide viewport, When any route renders, Then there is no horizontal scroll and nav remains usable.
Given OS dark mode, When the site renders, Then colors adapt with readable contrast in both themes.
ui_screens: Home page with the three feature entry points
ui_states: Route error (error boundary with disclaimer intact)
spec_items.accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA: semantic landmarks (header/nav/main/footer), skip-to-content link, visible focus states, contrast ≥ 4.5:1 both themes, nav operable by keyboard.
spec_items.responsive_behavior: Single-column at phone widths with compact nav; multi-column layouts only ≥ md breakpoint. No horizontal body scroll at any width ≥ 320px.
spec_items.content_i18n: English only. Plain-English register per BRD-004; all UI copy avoids finance jargon.
spec_items.performance_targets: App perf default (architecture decision record): LCP < 2.5s mid-range phone, Lighthouse perf ≥ 90 / a11y ≥ 95.
spec_items.security_requirements: No auth, no user input, no cookies. Static/server-rendered output only.
spec_items.test_strategy: Component render tests are low-value here; rely on e2e route checks + Lighthouse in SPEC-019. Verify every route renders with placeholder content (TASKS 2.1 check).
e2e_scenarios: Visit every top-level route; assert nav + disclaimer present and no horizontal overflow at 320px.
qa_signoff_criteria: All routes render inside shell
Disclaimer on every page
Dark/light both legible
spec_items.hypercare_watch: Vercel error rate on all routes; layout regressions reported via walkthrough.

spec_items.title: Data access layer: typed server-side query functions
spec_items.summary: One module of typed query functions — schools list, allocations by school, returns by school, market values, benchmarks by series, proxy mappings, sources — as the only DB touchpoint for pages.
assumptions: Purely technical enabler (no direct BRD requirement): centralizing queries keeps citation joins and coverage rules consistent across all three features.

api_contract.path: (internal function, not HTTP) getSchools / getAllocations(schoolId) / getReturns(schoolId) / getBenchmarks(series[]) / getProxyMappings() / getSources()
api_contract.request_shape: Typed params (schoolId: string, series: string[], fiscal-year ranges optional)
api_contract.response_shape: Typed rows matching schema.ts; allocation/return queries include source_id; numeric types normalized to number
error_codes: DB unreachable → thrown error caught by route error boundary

business_rules: Queries never filter out coverage gaps silently — missing years are returned as missing so charts can annotate them (BRD-005).
edge_cases: School with no allocation rows (Stanford)
Fiscal years present in returns but not allocations (Yale FY2021+)
Series with partial coverage (global_equity from FY2009)
error_handling: Connection errors propagate to the route error boundary; no silent empty-array fallbacks that would render misleading empty charts.
acceptance_criteria: Given the seeded DB, When each query function runs (exercised by tests or a debug page), Then real seeded rows return with correct types.
Given Stanford, When getAllocations runs, Then it returns an empty set (not an error) so the UI can render the OI-1 explanation.
spec_items.performance_targets: Each page's data needs served in ≤ 2 queries where practical; Neon HTTP driver latency accepted (app perf default governs page-level).
spec_items.security_requirements: Parameterized queries via Drizzle only; no string-built SQL; no user-supplied SQL fragments (inputs are ids/years validated against known sets).
spec_items.test_strategy: Integration tests against the dev database exercising each function, including the Stanford-empty and Yale-gap cases (TASKS 2.2 check: tests or debug page print real data).
integration_tests: getAllocations('yale') years span FY2000–FY2020 and each year sums ~100
qa_signoff_criteria: All integration tests green against seeded dev DB.

spec_items.title: Plain-English term definitions (first-use glossary component)
spec_items.summary: A reusable component + copy convention so every finance term is defined on first use per page — inline expandable definition or styled tooltip-equivalent that also works on touch and keyboard.
user_stories: As a smart 22-year-old outside finance, I want unfamiliar terms explained where they appear, so that I never have to leave the page to understand it.
business_rules: Definition copy comes from one shared glossary source (aligned with the BRD §10 glossary) so a term is defined identically everywhere.
First use per page gets the affordance; later uses may repeat it but must not omit a definition that page never gave.
edge_cases: Term inside a chart tooltip (define in adjacent prose instead)
Touch devices (tap to toggle, not hover-only)
Screen readers (definition exposed via accessible description, not title attribute)
error_handling: A term referenced without a glossary entry fails the build-time check (or lint script) rather than rendering undefined.
acceptance_criteria: Given a page using the term 'annualized return', When it first appears, Then a reader can reveal its plain-English definition without leaving the page, by mouse, touch, or keyboard.
Given a screen reader, When it encounters a defined term, Then the definition is announced via an accessible relationship.
spec_items.accessibility: Trigger is a real button; aria-expanded; definition programmatically associated; no hover-only interaction.
spec_items.responsive_behavior: Definitions render as inline expansion on narrow screens (no clipped floating tooltips).
spec_items.content_i18n: English only; definitions written at the BRD glossary register.
spec_items.test_strategy: Unit test the component's keyboard/touch toggle; the page-level 'no unexplained jargon' bar is enforced editorially in SPEC-018's plain-English pass.
unit_tests: Toggle by click, Enter, and Space; aria-expanded flips; definition text sourced from glossary module
qa_signoff_criteria: Component accessible per criteria; glossary module covers all BRD §10 terms.

spec_items.title: School picker and school page (story blurb + headline stats)
spec_items.summary: Explore entry: pick one of the five schools; each school page shows its plain-English story blurb (2–3 paragraphs, sourced facts only) and headline stats (latest market value, 10-yr and 25-yr annualized return where computable).
user_stories: As a DIY investor, I want to pick a school and get its investing story and key numbers at a glance, so that I can decide what to explore deeper.
preconditions: Database seeded with schools, returns, market values
main_flow: 3. School page renders: name, story blurb, headline stats, links/sections for the allocation and returns charts (SPEC-010/011/012)
business_rules: Blurbs contain sourced facts only, written fresh in plain English (2–3 paragraphs) — every factual claim traceable to a source on the methodology page.

Annualized returns computed by geometric compounding of fiscal-year returns; windows shown only where the full window of data exists (Stanford: return stats omitted per OI-1, market value shown instead).
No copy suggests the reader should invest like the school (BRD-002).
edge_cases: Stanford: no returns → headline stats show latest market value + 'returns unavailable' with OI-1 explanation link
10-yr window spans a school's missing return year (Princeton gaps) → omit the stat rather than bridge the gap
Unknown school slug in URL → 404 page
error_handling: Invalid school slug renders the not-found page; DB errors hit the route error boundary with disclaimer intact.
acceptance_criteria: Given the five schools, When each school page loads, Then blurb and headline stats render from DB data (TASKS 3.1 check).
Given Stanford's page, When it loads, Then latest market value shows, return stats are absent, and a plain-English note explains why with a methodology link.
Given a 25-yr annualized figure, When recomputed by hand from the seeded fiscal-year returns, Then it matches to 0.1pp.
spec_items.accessibility: Stats presented as labeled text (not color-only); blurb headings semantic; picker keyboard-navigable.
spec_items.responsive_behavior: Stats stack vertically at phone widths; picker becomes a vertical list.
spec_items.content_i18n: Plain English; 'annualized return' and 'market value' defined on first use via SPEC-008.
spec_items.performance_targets: App perf default; school pages are server-rendered and cacheable (data changes only at seed time).
spec_items.security_requirements: School slug validated against the known five before querying.
spec_items.test_strategy: Unit tests for the annualized-return helper (hand-computed values — financial math rule); e2e render check for all five school pages including the Stanford variant.
unit_tests: Geometric annualization matches hand-computed 3-year toy case
Window with a missing year returns 'not computable'
e2e_scenarios: Load all 5 school pages; assert blurb present, stats present (or Stanford variant), no unexplained jargon markers
qa_signoff_criteria: All 5 pages render from DB; stats hand-verified for one school; Stanford variant correct.

spec_items.title: Allocation-over-time chart with on-chart coverage-end annotation
spec_items.summary: Stacked-area allocation chart per school spanning that school's disclosed coverage, with the coverage end annotated on the chart itself (e.g. boundary marker: 'Yale last disclosed its allocation mix in FY2020'). Read the dataviz skill before writing any chart code.
preconditions: dataviz skill read in the building session (non-negotiable rule 5)
business_rules: Chart spans only the school's disclosed allocation coverage — never interpolate or extend (BRD-005).
Coverage end annotated on the chart itself, not a caption: the returns chart beside it runs to FY2025 and the reader needs the explanation at the moment they notice the mismatch (TASKS 3.2).
Categories use the normalized set with consistent colors across all schools (BRD-028).
edge_cases: Harvard's unpublished FY2018/FY2022 → visible gap or break, not interpolation
MIT's sparse years → chart must not imply continuity between distant points; consider discrete columns
Stanford → this chart does not render (SPEC-012 variant)
A school-year summing to 99.9/100.1 (tolerance) → normalize display to 100% stack with underlying values in tooltip
error_handling: Missing years render as explicit gaps with the same annotation pattern as the coverage end; tooltip shows fiscal year + category + pct + school's original label (sourceLabel) where space allows.
acceptance_criteria: Given Yale, When its allocation chart renders, Then it spans FY2000–FY2020 with a boundary marker labelled about FY2020 being the last disclosed mix (TASKS 3.2 check).
Given seeded data for any school-year, When compared to the chart tooltip, Then values match the DB exactly.
Given a 375px-wide phone, When the chart renders, Then labels and legend are legible and the chart scrolls or reflows without clipping.
spec_items.accessibility: Series distinguishable beyond hue alone (per dataviz skill); tooltip data available to keyboard/screen-reader users via an accessible table alternative of the same data.
spec_items.responsive_behavior: Legend wraps below chart at phone widths; chart height adapts; no horizontal body scroll.
spec_items.content_i18n: Annotation copy plain-English; 'asset allocation' defined on first use (SPEC-008).
spec_items.performance_targets: Chart data serialized server-side; client bundle only for the chart component. App perf default.
spec_items.test_strategy: Data-transform unit tests (DB rows → chart series, gap handling); visual/e2e check for the annotation and phone legibility. Chart rendering itself trusted to the library.
unit_tests: Yale transform ends at FY2020 and flags coverage end
Harvard transform emits explicit gaps at FY2018/FY2022
e2e_scenarios: Yale chart shows boundary annotation; tooltip matches a spot-checked seeded value
qa_signoff_criteria: Chart matches seeded data; coverage-end annotation on-chart; legible on phone (TASKS 3.2 checks).

spec_items.title: Annual returns chart (bar, with S&P 500 overlay toggle)
spec_items.summary: Per-school fiscal-year returns as a bar chart with a toggleable S&P 500 overlay; tooltip shows year + values.
business_rules: Negative years render plainly (below axis) — honesty over narrative (BRD-005).
Overlay compares identical fiscal-year windows (benchmarks are FY-aligned, BRD-027).
edge_cases: Princeton's missing return years → visible gap, annotated like SPEC-010
Stanford → chart replaced by the SPEC-012 unavailable-state
Overlay toggled on for a school whose coverage is shorter than the S&P series → overlay clipped to the school's window
error_handling: Tooltip always shows fiscal year + both values when overlay is on; missing school year shows 'not published' rather than 0.
acceptance_criteria: Given any school with returns, When the chart renders, Then bar values match the DB (TASKS 3.3 check) and tooltips show year + value(s).

spec_items.title: Backtest engine (pure functions + hand-computed unit tests)
spec_items.summary: The most correctness-critical code in the app: given {category, pct} weights, map to proxy series via proxy_mappings and compute year-by-year portfolio returns FY-to-FY with annual rebalancing, growth of $10k, annualized return, best/worst year. Pure functions, no I/O.
spec_items.detailed_description: Annual rebalancing means each fiscal year the portfolio return is the weight-dot-product of that year's proxy-series returns (weights reset every year). Growth of $10k compounds those yearly returns. Annualized return is the geometric mean. Where SPEC-005 decided a category has no proxy (explicit-gap sleeve), the engine computes on the replicable sleeve renormalized to 100% and reports the uncovered fraction so the UI can label the gap — it must never silently renormalize without reporting.
business_rules: Annual rebalancing only; no taxes or fees modeled — and the fine print says so (BRD-014).
Computed strictly from stored annual series (BRD-013); the engine takes series as inputs and performs no I/O.
Uncovered (no-proxy) allocation fraction is always returned alongside results, never swallowed.
A requested window containing a year with a missing proxy-series value fails loudly (returns an explicit 'not computable for FYxxxx') rather than skipping the year.
edge_cases: Weights not summing to exactly 100 (seed tolerance ±0.1) → normalize and record the adjustment
Single-year window (annualized = that year's return)
Negative-return years in best/worst detection
Category with zero weight
Window entirely before a proxy series' first covered year
error_handling: Invalid inputs (empty weights, unknown category, reversed year range) throw typed errors with plain messages; UI layers translate them to friendly copy.
acceptance_criteria: Given the 60/40 weights and seeded sp500/us_aggregate_bond series, When the engine runs FY2000–FY2025, Then yearly returns match hand-computed values exactly and the growth-of-$10k endpoint matches to the cent (TASKS 4.1 check).
Given a 3-year toy dataset computed by hand, When the engine runs, Then yearly portfolio returns, growth series, annualized return, and best/worst year all match the hand computation.
Given a portfolio with an uncovered category, When the engine runs, Then results carry the uncovered fraction and the sleeve-renormalization is explicit in the output.
spec_items.performance_targets: Pure in-memory math over ≤ 26 years × ≤ 8 categories — negligible; must be callable in server components without caching concerns.
spec_items.security_requirements: No I/O, no user-controlled strings — inputs validated to known categories/series upstream.
spec_items.test_strategy: Unit tests with hand-computed expected values are mandatory (CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 6). Cover the toy case, the 60/40 real-data case, and every edge case listed. No mocks needed — pure functions.
unit_tests: Hand-computed 3-year toy portfolio: yearly returns, growth series, annualized, best/worst
60/40 FY case matching TASKS 1.4's Vanguard cross-check window
Uncovered-sleeve renormalization reports the gap fraction

Weights summing to 99.9 → normalized with adjustment recorded
qa_signoff_criteria: All unit tests green; a reviewer re-derives the toy case by hand and matches.
spec_items.hypercare_watch: None at runtime (deterministic math); regressions guarded by tests.

risk_register.risk: Sparse/gapped school data (MIT, Princeton, Harvard) renders misleadingly if charts imply continuity
risk_register.mitigation: Explicit-gap rendering rules in SPEC-010/011; no interpolation ever; coverage stories on methodology page

open_questions.question: Final call on the hedge-fund / private-equity sleeve: explicit-gap (copycat covers only the publicly-replicable sleeve, remainder shown as a labelled gap) vs. any liquid-alt stand-in?
open_questions.context: Decides SPEC-005's curation and shapes SPEC-013 engine output and SPEC-014/015 labelling. TASKS 1.7 already frames explicit-gap as 'likely more honest' and no freely-citable investable series reaches FY2000.
open_questions.proposed_default: Explicit-gap sleeve, per the architecture decision record and TASKS 1.7 framing.
open_questions.resolution: Resolved 2026-08-04 by owner: explicit-gap sleeve confirmed — the copycat covers only the publicly-replicable sleeve; hedge funds / private equity render as a labelled gap, never a stand-in proxy.

open_questions.question: Confirm Recharts as the chart library (PRD default suggestion), or pick another well-maintained React chart library at build time?
open_questions.context: Affects SPEC-010/011/012/015/016 implementation and bundle size. The dataviz skill governs the design either way.
open_questions.proposed_default: Recharts, unless the dataviz-skill review at M3 surfaces a concrete blocker (e.g. accessible-table alternative friction).

open_questions.question: Add lightweight observability (Vercel Analytics / Speed Insights, both Pro-included) and a test step in CI, or keep hypercare monitoring manual via Vercel logs?
open_questions.context: Hypercare_plan monitoring currently relies on manual daily checks of Vercel logs; Pro plan includes analytics toggles that need only dashboard enablement (human).
open_questions.proposed_default: Enable Vercel Analytics + Speed Insights at M6 (human toggles, one-line code add); keep CI as local pre-push tests for v1.

glossary.definition: A university's long-term investment fund, built from donations, that pays out a slice each year to support the school.
How a portfolio is divided among investment types (stocks, bonds, real estate, etc.), usually percentages summing to 100.
A school's 12-month accounting year. FY2025 = July 2024–June 2025 for four schools; Sep 2024–Aug 2025 for Stanford.
Exchange-traded fund — a fund holding a basket of investments that trades on a stock exchange like a single share.
A simple reference portfolio (like the S&P 500) used as a yardstick for performance.
The single per-year growth rate that would produce the same overall result as the actual year-by-year returns.
Periodically trading back to target allocation after market moves; this project models it once per year.
The DIY version of an endowment's allocation built from ordinary ETFs standing in for each asset class.
The total dollar size of the endowment at fiscal-year end.
Stanford's commingled investment vehicle; larger than and distinct from the endowment itself (see BRD OI-1).
A school's allocation mix from a specific year, held unchanged by the copycat in forward runs past that year.
The honest handling of unreplicable categories (hedge funds, private equity): the copycat covers only what ordinary ETFs can replicate and labels the remainder as a gap instead of faking a proxy.
